==English==
{{wp|<dab!>}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|travail|travell||obsolete}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈtɹævəl/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-travel.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ævəl|s=2}}

===Etymology 1===
{{PIE word|en|tréyes}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂ǵ-}}
{{rfc|en|Middle Scots comes after Middle English.}}
From {{inh|en|enm|travelen|t=to make a laborious journey, travel}} from {{der|en|gmw-msc|travailen|t=to toil, work, travel}}, alteration of {{cog|enm|travaillen|t=to toil, work}}, from {{der|en|fro|travailler|t=to trouble, suffer, be worn out}}. See the {{glossary|doublet}}s {{doublet|en|travail|travois|notext=1}}.

Compare typologically {{m|en|routine}} << {{m+|la|rupta via}}. Note the inverse semantic vectors: ''travel'' moves from a subjective state (toil) to an objective action (journey), while ''routine'' moves from an objective object (beaten path) to a subjective pattern (habit).

Largely displaced native {{m|en|fare}}, from {{cog|ang|faran|t=to go [a long distance], to travel}}. More at {{m|en|fare}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|+l}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be on a [[journey]], often for pleasure or business and with luggage; to go from one place to another.
#: {{ux|en|John seems to spend as much time '''travelling''' as he does in the office.}}
#: {{ux|en|Snakes do not '''travel''' well.}}
#: {{ux|en|I still '''travel''' to work by bus.}}
#* {{quote-web
|en
|date=2012-06-09
|author=Owen Phillips
|title=Euro 2012: Netherlands 0-1 Denmark
|work=w:BBC Sport
|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/18138777
|page=
|passage=And Netherlands, backed by a typically noisy and colourful '''travelling''' support, started the second period in blistering fashion and could have had four goals within 10 minutes|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220215144453/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/18138777}}
#* {{RQ:NYPost|author=Snejana Farberov|title=Dad shot dead in road-rage attack after splashing windshield fluid on BMW|url=https://nypost.com/2022/07/21/dad-shot-dead-after-splashing-windshield-fluid-on-bmw/|date=2022-07-21|passage=Dennis Anderson, 45, and Brandy Goldsbury, 46, were '''traveling''' from the beach in Lincoln City on the Oregon coast back to their home in Tigard around 8:30 p.m. July 13 when they spotted a black BMW 3 Series trying to pass them, according to reporting in The Oregonian.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816233207/https://nypost.com/2022/07/21/dad-shot-dead-after-splashing-windshield-fluid-on-bmw/}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[pass]] from one place to another; to move or [[transmit]].
#: {{syn|en|range<qq:ballistics>}}
#: {{ux|en|Soundwaves can '''travel''' through water.}}
#: {{ux|en|The supposedly secret news of Mary's engagement '''travelled''' quickly through her group of friends.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|basketball}} To move illegally by walking or running without dribbling the ball.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To travel throughout (a place).
#: {{ux|en|I’ve '''travelled''' the world.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To force to journey.
#* {{RQ:Spenser Ireland|passage=They shall not be '''travailed''' forth of their own franchises.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[labour]]; to [[travail]].

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|travail}}, {{m|enm|travell}}, from {{der|en|fro|travail}}, {{m|fro|travaille}}, {{m|fro|travaillie}}, {{m|fro|traval}}, {{m|fro|travalle}}, {{m|fro|traveaul}}, {{m|fro|traveil}}, {{m|fro|traveille}}, {{m|fro|travel}}. {{doublet|en|travail}}.

====Noun====
[[File:Caravane de Méharis dans le Hoggar.jpg|thumb|A [[caravan]] [[en route]]]]
{{en-noun|~}}

# The act of traveling; passage from place to place.
#: {{ux|en|I like '''travel''', but it’s always too tiring.}}
#: {{ux|en|[[space travel|space '''travel''']]}}
#: {{ux|en|a '''travel''' iron}}
# {{lb|en|in the plural}} A series of [[journey]]s.
#: {{ux|en|I’m off on my '''travels''' around France again.}}
# {{lb|en|in the plural}} An account of one's travels.
#: {{ux|en|He released his '''travels''' in 1900, two years after returning from Africa.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1903|author=Henry Yule; Arthur Burnell|title=Hobson-Jobson
|passage=CALUAT, s. This in some old '''travels''' is used for Ar. khilwat, 'privacy, a private interview' (C. P. Brown, MS.).}}
# The activity or traffic along a route or through a given point.
# The working motion of a piece of machinery; the length of a mechanical stroke.
#: {{ux|en|There was a lot of '''travel''' in the handle, because the tool was out of adjustment.}}
#: {{ux|en|My drill press has a '''travel''' of only 1.5 inches.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Labour; [[parturition]]; [[travail]].
# {{C|en|Typing keyboards}} Distance that a keyboard's key moves vertically when depressed.
#: {{ux|en|The keys have great '''travel'''.}}

=====Usage notes=====
* Used attributively to describe things that have been created or modified for use during a journey.
